metaTitle: Real-Time Analytics: The Definitive Guide for Data Lakehouse
metaDescription: Learn what real-time analytics means in the data lakehouse, how streaming ingestion and query engines like Dremio enable near-real-time dashboards on Apache Iceberg data.
lede: Real-time analytics delivers business insights from data that is seconds to minutes old — enabling live operational dashboards, real-time fraud detection, and immediate response to business events. In the lakehouse, real-time analytics combines streaming ingestion (Flink → Iceberg) with fast query execution (Dremio Reflections) to close the gap between event and insight.

faqs.q: What is real-time analytics in the data lakehouse?
faqs.a: Real-time analytics in the data lakehouse refers to querying data that is updated continuously from operational systems — within seconds to minutes of events occurring — rather than querying historical batch-loaded data. It requires both a real-time ingestion pipeline (Kafka → Flink → Iceberg) and a fast query engine (Dremio with Reflections) that can serve queries on frequently updated tables with sub-second latency.

faqs.q: How does Dremio enable real-time analytics on Iceberg?
faqs.a: Dremio enables near-real-time analytics through two mechanisms: Reflections that refresh frequently (every few minutes) to pre-compute aggregations on recently ingested data, and direct Iceberg scan mode for the most current data where Reflection staleness is unacceptable. The combination delivers sub-second BI performance on data that may be only minutes old.

faqs.q: What is the difference between real-time and near-real-time analytics?
faqs.a: True real-time analytics (millisecond freshness) requires OLAP databases designed for high-frequency writes (ClickHouse, Apache Druid). Near-real-time analytics (second to minute freshness) is achievable in the lakehouse using streaming ingestion to Iceberg + fast query engines. Most business use cases labeled 'real-time' actually need near-real-time — a 2-minute-old fraud dashboard is operationally effective for most fraud teams.

sections.heading: What Is Real-Time Analytics?
sections.content:
Real-time analytics is the capability to query and analyze data that is continuously updated from source systems, delivering insights from events that occurred seconds to minutes ago — rather than from batch-loaded data that may be hours or days old. Real-time analytics enables operational use cases that require current data: fraud detection dashboards, live inventory monitoring, customer journey analysis, operational SLA tracking, and real-time A/B test result monitoring.

In the data lakehouse, real-time analytics is achieved by combining a streaming ingestion pipeline (Kafka → Flink → Bronze Iceberg tables) with a fast analytical query engine (Dremio with Reflections). The result is a lakehouse that serves BI queries on data that may be only 1–5 minutes old — sufficient for the vast majority of operational analytics use cases.

sections.heading: The Near-Real-Time Lakehouse Stack
sections.content:
The near-real-time lakehouse architecture:

  1. Event sources: Operational databases (via Debezium CDC), application services (direct Kafka producers), and external APIs publish events to Kafka topics
  2. Flink ingestion: Flink reads Kafka topics and writes to Bronze Iceberg tables with Iceberg's streaming write mode — committing new snapshots every 1–5 minutes (configurable)
  3. Dremio Reflection refresh: Dremio's Reflection refresh schedule detects new Iceberg snapshots and refreshes relevant Aggregation Reflections — typically completing in 15–60 seconds for small incremental snapshots
  4. BI queries served: BI tools querying Dremio receive results from the refreshed Reflection — data is 2–7 minutes old end-to-end

sections.heading: When the Lakehouse is Enough vs Specialized OLAP
sections.content:
The lakehouse near-real-time approach is sufficient for most operational analytics use cases. Specialized real-time OLAP databases (Apache Druid, ClickHouse, Apache Pinot) provide true real-time query on data updated at very high frequency (millions of events/second, second-level freshness requirements), but at the cost of a separate system with its own storage, management, and data duplication.

For most organizations, the near-real-time lakehouse (2–5 minute data freshness on Iceberg + Dremio) eliminates the need for a separate real-time OLAP tier — reducing architectural complexity while delivering freshness levels that are operationally effective for fraud, operations, and business monitoring use cases.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.content: Real-time analytics in the data lakehouse is achievable through the combination of streaming ingestion (Flink writing to Iceberg every few minutes) and fast query execution (Dremio serving Reflection-accelerated queries on the most recent snapshots). For most operational analytics use cases, this near-real-time lakehouse approach delivers sufficient freshness while maintaining the governance, openness, and analytical richness of the full lakehouse platform — without requiring a separate real-time OLAP database and its associated operational complexity.
